name: WK Kellogg Co
group: Subsidiaries: consumer and media companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Maker of Kellogg's breakfast cereals in North America, including Frosted Flakes, Froot Loops and Raisin Bran.
capacity_detail: Bought by Ferrero for USD 3.1bn; deal closed 26 September 2025
markets: Cereals sold mainly in the United States, Canada and the Caribbean under Kellogg's brands.
rationale: Iconic family cereal brands could use F1's fast-growing US fan base to reach young families and modernise the brand.

name: Kellanova
group: Subsidiaries: consumer and media companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Maker of snack and convenience foods including Pringles, Cheez-It, Pop-Tarts and Eggo, now owned by Mars.
capacity_detail: Acquired by Mars in a USD 36bn deal, completed 11 December 2025; revenue USD 12.7bn in 2024
markets: Snack brands sold worldwide; offices in Chicago, Battle Creek and a European headquarters in Dublin.
rationale: Pringles is a global snack brand aimed at young adults; F1's worldwide audience fits its sharing and gaming occasions.

name: Foot Locker
group: Subsidiaries: consumer and media companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Mall-based retailer of sneakers and athletic apparel with over 2,500 stores across more than 40 countries.
capacity_detail: Bought by Dick's Sporting Goods for USD 2.4bn, completed 8 September 2025; revenue USD 8.15bn in 2023
sponsorships: Foot Locker Cross Country Championships; Foot Locker Scholar Athletes
markets: More than 40 countries across the United States, Canada, Europe and Asia; brands include Kids Foot Locker and House of Hoops.
rationale: Sneaker culture and F1's young fan base overlap; F1 merchandise and footwear drops could drive store traffic.

name: Siete Foods
group: Subsidiaries: consumer and media companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Mexican-American food brand making grain-free tortillas, tortilla chips and related grocery products.
capacity_detail: Acquired by PepsiCo for USD 1.2bn; completion announced 17 January 2025
markets: Sold in United States grocery retail; founded in Texas.
rationale: PepsiCo already uses F1; Siete could join activations aimed at US Hispanic fans around Austin and Mexico City races.

name: Poppi
group: Subsidiaries: consumer and media companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Prebiotic soda brand selling low-sugar fruit-flavoured sparkling drinks, launched in the UK and Ireland in 2026.
capacity_detail: PepsiCo announced it would acquire Poppi for USD 1.95bn; completed 19 May 2025
markets: United States, and since 2026 the United Kingdom and Ireland.
rationale: A young, social-media-led drinks brand expanding abroad could ride F1's Gen Z audience and parent PepsiCo's F1 rights.

name: Dr. Squatch
group: Subsidiaries: consumer and media companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Men's personal-care brand selling natural bar soaps, deodorant and grooming products online and in stores.
capacity_detail: Acquired by Unilever from Summit Partners for USD 1.5bn; completed 16 November 2025
markets: Mainly the United States, sold online by subscription and in physical retail stores.
rationale: A male-focused grooming brand with humorous marketing matches F1's largely male, young audience as it grows abroad.

name: Rhode
group: Subsidiaries: consumer and media companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Skincare and makeup brand founded by Hailey Bieber, sold online and through Sephora in several countries.
capacity_detail: Bought by e.l.f. Beauty in a USD 1bn deal (USD 800M at closing plus USD 200M earnout); completed August 2025; revenue USD 212M in year to March 2025
markets: United States, Canada, United Kingdom and Australia via its website and Sephora.
rationale: A fast-growing beauty brand courting young women could use F1's growing female audience and lifestyle events.

name: Britvic
group: Subsidiaries: consumer and media companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: British soft-drinks maker and bottler of brands such as Robinsons and J2O, now part of Carlsberg Britvic.
ownership: subsidiary of Carlsberg Group (Britvic Ltd within Carlsberg Britvic)
capacity_detail: Bought by Carlsberg for GBP 3.3bn, completed 17 January 2025; revenue GBP 1,899M in 2024
markets: United Kingdom and Ireland, with Britvic-branded soft drinks sold in other markets.
rationale: A British drinks maker could use the British Grand Prix and UK-based teams for hospitality and soft-drink activations.

name: Courvoisier
group: Subsidiaries: consumer and media companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Cognac house based in Jarnac, France, producing and selling Courvoisier cognac worldwide.
capacity_detail: Bought by Campari from Beam Suntory for USD 1.2bn; completion announced 1 May 2024
markets: Cognac sold worldwide; boutique and museum at the Courvoisier Château in Jarnac.
rationale: Premium spirits brands use F1 hospitality and luxury positioning; cognac rivals like Hennessy's group already sponsor F1.

name: Hawaiian Airlines
group: Subsidiaries: consumer and media companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Airline serving Hawaii with flights to the US mainland, Asia and the Pacific, now operated by Alaska.
capacity_detail: Bought by Alaska Air Group for USD 1.9bn cash plus about USD 900M debt; closed 18 September 2024; revenue USD 3.3bn in 2025
markets: 31 destinations between Hawaii, the US mainland, Asia and the South Pacific.
rationale: A leisure airline linking Asia-Pacific and US races could promote Hawaii travel to F1's affluent, international audience.

name: Vizio
group: Subsidiaries: consumer and media companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Consumer electronics brand selling smart televisions and soundbars, now a Walmart-owned brand.
capacity_detail: Bought by Walmart for USD 2.3bn; completed 3 December 2024
sponsorships: Rose Bowl and Fiesta Bowl title sponsor (past)
markets: North America; becoming a brand sold only at Walmart and Sam's Club.
rationale: A TV brand selling home viewing could use F1's growing US TV audience to show screens built for live sport.

name: Hibbett
group: Subsidiaries: consumer and media companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Sporting goods retailer selling athletic footwear and apparel through more than 1,100 stores in 36 US states.
capacity_detail: Bought by JD Sports for USD 1.08bn, completed July 2024; revenue USD 1.73bn (year to Feb 2024)
markets: United States: 1,169 stores in 36 states under Hibbett, City Gear and Sports Additions.
rationale: Sneaker retail aimed at young Americans could tie into F1's US growth and merchandise demand.

name: Mattress Firm
group: Subsidiaries: consumer and media companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Specialty mattress retailer with about 2,300 US stores, now owned by Tempur Sealy's parent Somnigroup.
capacity_detail: Bought by Tempur Sealy (now Somnigroup) in a USD 4bn deal (USD 5bn as closed); completed February 2025
markets: United States, about 2,300 locations; delivery partnership with DoorDash.
rationale: Sleep and recovery messaging links to driver performance; Eight Sleep already shows the angle in F1.

name: JioStar
group: Subsidiaries: consumer and media companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Indian media group running Star and Colors TV channels, Star Sports and the JioHotstar streaming platform.
ownership: subsidiary of Reliance Industries (63.16%: 16.34% direct and 46.82% via Viacom18); Disney holds 36.84%
capacity_detail: Merger of Viacom18 and Disney Star completed 14 November 2024, valued at USD 8.5bn; revenue about USD 2.8bn (FY2024)
sponsorships: Media rights holder for IPL and US Open tennis (not sponsorships)
markets: India: more than 100 TV channels, Star Sports and the JioHotstar streaming service.
rationale: India's largest sports broadcaster could co-promote F1 content and target Indian fans through JioHotstar.

name: Tegna
group: Subsidiaries: consumer and media companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: American local television broadcaster owning stations across US markets, now a Nexstar subsidiary.
capacity_detail: Bought by Nexstar for USD 6.2bn, closed 19 March 2026; revenue USD 2.71bn in 2025
markets: United States local TV markets; kept separate from Nexstar under an April 2026 court injunction.
rationale: Local TV stations could host race-weekend content for US Grands Prix, but brand sponsorship need is limited.

name: GetGo
group: Subsidiaries: consumer and media companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Chain of convenience stores and fuel stations, run by Couche-Tard as a business separate from Circle K.
capacity_detail: Bought from Giant Eagle by Couche-Tard in a USD 1.57bn acquisition; sale closed 29 June 2025
markets: 277 stores (2023) in the US Midwest and mid-Atlantic.
rationale: Fuel and food stores reach drivers; motorsport themes suit fuel retail, though the regional footprint limits value.

name: Champion
group: Subsidiaries: consumer and media companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: American sportswear brand selling athletic apparel and streetwear, owned and marketed by Authentic Brands.
capacity_detail: Bought by Authentic Brands from HanesBrands for USD 1.2bn; completed September 2024
sponsorships: NBL (Australia) apparel partner; licensed NFL and NHL apparel; UFC fighter Tom Aspinall
markets: North America, Europe, Asia and Brazil.
rationale: A heritage sportswear brand reviving through sport licensing could use F1 team kit and lifestyle capsules.

name: Depop
group: Subsidiaries: consumer and media companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Online marketplace app for buying and selling second-hand fashion, popular with young users.
capacity_detail: Sold by Etsy to eBay for USD 1.2bn cash; completed July 2026 after UK CMA approval
markets: United Kingdom, United States and Italy; offices in London, Milan, Los Angeles and New York; 56.3M users.
rationale: Gen Z resale fashion matches F1's young fanbase; team merchandise resale and style content are a natural fit.

name: Dorna Sports (MotoGP)
group: Subsidiaries: consumer and media companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Owner and promoter of the MotoGP and WorldSBK motorcycle racing world championships.
ownership: subsidiary of Liberty Media (84%); MotoGP management holds 16%
capacity_detail: Liberty Media agreed to buy 86% for EUR 4.2bn (about USD 4.5bn); completed 3 July 2025
markets: Worldwide championships: MotoGP, WorldSBK, WorldWCR and Bagger World Cup.
rationale: Shares an owner with F1, so a sponsorship makes little sense; listed for completeness only.
parent_f1: owner of a current F1 partner (owner of Formula 1)

name: BRF
group: Subsidiaries: consumer and media companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Brazilian food producer of poultry, pork and processed foods under brands including Sadia and Perdigão.
ownership: subsidiary of MBRF Global Foods (formed by merger with Marfrig, September 2025)
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 10.8bn in 2023
sponsorships: Sadia: Rio 2016 Olympics sponsor; Brazil national football team sponsor 2013-2016 (past)
markets: Sells in Brazil and export markets; more than 30 brands including Sadia, Perdigão, Qualy and Bocatti.
rationale: Sadia's past Olympic and football deals show appetite; F1's São Paulo and Middle East races match key markets.

name: GOJO Industries
group: Subsidiaries: consumer and media companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Maker of Purell hand sanitizer plus hand soaps, skin care, surgical scrubs and dispensers sold worldwide.
capacity_detail: Bought by Clorox for USD 2.25bn cash; acquisition completed in 2026 (1 April per Wikipedia)
markets: Sold worldwide; offices in the UK, France, Australia, Japan and Brazil; factories in the Americas, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Purell hygiene stations at circuits and in team garages could showcase health messaging to crowds at mass events.

name: Huel
group: Subsidiaries: consumer and media companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: British maker of nutritionally complete powders, shakes, meals and bars sold mostly direct to consumers.
capacity_detail: Danone deal valued Huel at EUR 1bn (March 2026); Danone announced completion 4 September 2026; revenue over GBP 200M (year to July 2024)
markets: United Kingdom, Europe and the United States, sold mainly direct to consumers online.
rationale: A performance-nutrition brand for busy, active adults suits F1's fitness and driver-preparation storytelling.

name: Alani Nu
group: Subsidiaries: consumer and media companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Energy drink and wellness supplement brand aimed at young women, owned by Celsius Holdings.
capacity_detail: Celsius announced a USD 1.8bn cash-and-stock deal (Feb 2025); PitchBook data says Celsius acquired Alani Nu on 1 April 2025
markets: Mainly the United States.
rationale: Celsius already sponsors Aston Martin; Alani Nu could use F1's growing female audience for energy-drink activations.
parent_f1: owner of a current F1 partner (Celsius)

name: Coca-Cola Europacific Aboitiz Philippines
group: Subsidiaries: consumer and media companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Bottler and distributor of Coca-Cola soft drinks in the Philippines, renamed in January 2025 after its sale.
ownership: subsidiary of Coca-Cola Europacific Partners (60%); Aboitiz Equity Ventures holds 40%
capacity_detail: Bought jointly by CCEP (60%) and Aboitiz Equity Ventures (40%) from The Coca-Cola Company for USD 1.8bn; announced as acquired 23 February 2024
markets: The Philippines.
rationale: A bottler sells Coca-Cola's brands, so its own sponsorship use is limited to local trade promotions.

name: Seiyu
group: Subsidiaries: consumer and media companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Nationwide Japanese supermarket chain, formerly owned by Walmart and KKR, now part of Trial Holdings.
capacity_detail: Trial Holdings' takeover valued Seiyu at about JPY 382.6bn (roughly USD 2.5bn); completed 1 July 2025
markets: Japan: about 330 supermarkets nationwide (2021).
rationale: A mass grocery chain could run F1-themed promotions around the Suzuka Grand Prix, though its reach is purely Japanese.

name: Snaitech
group: Subsidiaries: consumer and media companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Italian betting and gaming operator running Snai betting shops, online gaming and sports media channels.
capacity_detail: Flutter agreed a EUR 2.3bn deal for Snaitech (Sept 2024); Snaitech's site now states it has joined Flutter Entertainment
sponsorships: Partnerships with AC Milan and AS Roma (announced 2017 or earlier; current status not shown)
markets: Italy: betting shops, online betting and gaming, plus Snai Sport and EQUtv media.
rationale: Italian betting brand could target Monza race fans, but Italian gambling advertising bans limit sports sponsorship.
parent_f1: owner of a current F1 partner (FanDuel)

name: Easybrain
group: Subsidiaries: consumer and media companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Mobile game developer of casual puzzle games such as Sudoku.com, sold by Embracer to Miniclip.
ownership: subsidiary of Miniclip, which is majority-owned by Tencent
capacity_detail: Embracer sold Easybrain to Miniclip for USD 1.2bn; transaction closed 22 January 2025
markets: Mobile puzzle games played worldwide through app stores.
rationale: Casual mobile games reach huge global audiences; F1-themed in-game events could fit, though brand-building need is modest.
parent_f1: owner of a current F1 partner (PUBG Mobile (publisher))

name: FANCL
group: Subsidiaries: consumer and media companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Japanese maker of additive-free cosmetics and health supplements, now wholly owned by Kirin.
capacity_detail: Kirin's tender offer for the shares it did not own totalled about JPY 220bn (roughly USD 1.4bn), completed 19 September 2024; revenue JPY 110.9bn in year to March 2024
markets: Japan, where it sells cosmetics and supplements; Kirin owns it as part of its health business.
rationale: A health and beauty brand under Kirin could use the Japanese Grand Prix to reach affluent consumers, but fit is weak.

name: Creed
group: Subsidiaries: consumer and media companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Luxury fragrance house selling perfumes through its own boutiques worldwide, now part of L'Oréal's luxury division.
ownership: subsidiary of L'Oréal (bought with Kering Beauté)
capacity_detail: L'Oréal completed buying Kering Beauté, including Creed, on 31 March 2026; PitchBook data lists Creed Fragrances acquired by L'Oréal for USD 4.6bn
markets: Boutiques in many cities worldwide; part of L'Oréal Luxe.
rationale: A heritage luxury fragrance house could use F1's Monaco, Abu Dhabi and Las Vegas glamour to reach wealthy buyers.
parent_f1: owner of a current F1 partner (SkinCeuticals)

name: Mainland Group
group: Subsidiaries: consumer and media companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Former Fonterra consumer dairy business selling Anchor, Mainland and Anlene butter, cheese and milk products.
capacity_detail: Fonterra's consumer dairy business acquired by Lactalis for USD 4.2bn in March 2026 (PitchBook); agreed price NZD 3.85bn
markets: New Zealand, Australia and other Asia-Pacific markets for Anchor, Mainland and Anlene brands.
rationale: Anchor and Anlene sell across Asia-Pacific; F1's Melbourne, Singapore and Shanghai races reach those consumers.

name: ISDIN
group: Subsidiaries: consumer and media companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Dermocosmetics company specialising in sun protection and dermatological skincare, now fully owned by Puig.
capacity_detail: Puig bought the remaining 50% from Esteve for about USD 1.4bn in September 2026, ending 50 years of joint ownership
markets: Dermocosmetic products sold through pharmacies; reach beyond Spain not detailed on the page read.
rationale: A sun-protection brand fits outdoor sport; F1's sunny races could promote skin protection to fans in hot climates.

name: Atlético Madrid
group: Subsidiaries: consumer and media companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Spanish La Liga football club, majority-owned since March 2026 by Apollo Sports Capital.
ownership: private equity: Apollo Sports Capital (55%); Quantum Pacific Group 25%
capacity_detail: Apollo's controlling-stake deal valued the club at about EUR 2.2bn, finalised March 2026; revenue EUR 409.5M in 2023-24
sponsorships: Shirt sponsors include Riyadh Air (2023-24) and Visit Rwanda (2025 onward); Nike kit since 2001
markets: Spain-based club with a worldwide fan base through La Liga and the UEFA Champions League.
rationale: Football clubs and F1 teams share sponsors; a club-team tie-up could cross-sell fans in Spain and Latin America.

name: PrizePicks
group: Subsidiaries: consumer and media companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Daily fantasy sports app, the largest such operator in North America, majority-owned by lottery group Allwyn.
capacity_detail: Allwyn completed the purchase of a 62.3% stake for about USD 1.5bn (announced 16 January 2026)
sponsorships: Official daily fantasy partner of the Atlanta Braves (2024); State Farm Arena marketing partnership (2024)
markets: United States and North America; fantasy contests on major sports and esports.
rationale: Sister brand Allwyn already partners F1; PrizePicks could add F1 fantasy contests to reach US fans.

name: FineToday
group: Subsidiaries: consumer and media companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Tokyo-based maker of skincare and haircare products, bought from CVC by Bain Capital in 2026.
capacity_detail: Bain Capital acquired FineToday from CVC Capital Partners for USD 1.3bn in June 2026 (PitchBook data)
markets: Japan, with personal-care products; wider markets not detailed on the page read.
rationale: A mass beauty brand could use the Japanese Grand Prix to reach young consumers, though fit is modest.
